security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown inline code, fenced examples, and TypeScript snippets rather than executable code. The confirmed concern is the pnpm workflow combined with Bash permission, because project scripts can run arbitrary repository code. No prompt injection, credential handling, data exfiltration, or suspicious external network destination was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Package script execution through pnpm commands
remediation.suggestion: State that pnpm scripts should run only after reviewing package scripts and receiving user confirmation in untrusted repositories.
Limit Bash usage to named development commands or document that command execution depends on the host approval policy.

content.value_statement: TypeScript teams need consistent rules for quality, typing, documentation, and review. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a concise TypeScript workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines a pnpm-first workflow for formatting, linting, type checks, and tests.
Recommends strict TypeScript settings, ES module imports, and safer null handling.
Provides a review checklist for TSDoc, error handling, tests, and type safety.
Shows guidance for Result patterns, type guards, and async error handling.
Suggests React memoization, lazy loading, and type-only imports.
Identifies common anti-patterns such as any, implicit any, and excessive assertions.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not include automation scripts.
It assumes pnpm, which may not match every TypeScript project.
It does not replace ESLint, TypeScript compiler checks, or test suites.
Bash-enabled workflows require care when repositories are untrusted.

use_cases.title: Review TypeScript Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist for typing, TSDoc, imports, error handling, and tests before merge.

use_cases.title: Set Team TypeScript Standards
use_cases.description: Define reusable rules for pnpm usage, strict compiler settings, documentation, and review expectations.

use_cases.title: Improve React TypeScript Components
use_cases.description: Check memoization, lazy loading, type-only imports, and safer async patterns in component work.

prompt_templates.title: Review a TypeScript File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the open TypeScript file for strict typing, error handling, TSDoc needs, and any usage. Summarize issues before edits.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist for this TypeScript pull request using the skill rules. Include type safety, tests, documentation, imports, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Safer Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript module toward stricter types without changing behavior. Prefer inferred types where clear and explain each risky change.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a TypeScript Quality Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this TypeScript project for type safety, documentation, React performance, and package workflow risks. Propose staged changes and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Review a new TypeScript service before merge.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review summary covering type safety, error handling, documentation needs, test coverage, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Plan cleanup for a React TypeScript component.
output_examples.output: A short plan covering memoization, lazy loading, async handling, type-only imports, and unnecessary assertions.

output_examples.input: Prepare team standards for a TypeScript project.
output_examples.output: A concise standards checklist for pnpm, strict compiler settings, TSDoc, imports, and review expectations.

best_practices: Use the skill when working on TypeScript or TSX files that need review or cleanup.
Ask for a summary of risks before accepting code changes.
Confirm package-script commands before running them in unfamiliar repositories.
anti_patterns: Running package scripts from untrusted repositories without reviewing them first.
Treating the examples as a complete architecture for every project.
Ignoring existing project standards when they conflict with the skill guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill itself is guidance. In agent environments with Bash enabled, command execution depends on the host approval policy.

faq.question: Does it support JavaScript projects?
faq.answer: It is designed for TypeScript and TSX projects. Some review ideas may still help JavaScript teams.

faq.question: Does the skill require pnpm?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow prefers pnpm and tells users not to use npm or yarn.

faq.question: Does it replace compiler and lint checks?
faq.answer: No. It complements TypeScript, ESLint, formatters, and tests with review guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with React TypeScript code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for memoization, lazy loading, hooks, and type-only imports.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Package scripts can execute repository code, so review scripts and confirm commands before running them.
